cards.back: Random → no bias; representative → reflects the population; enough samples → reliable. Bias sources: convenience samples, leading questions.
Mean = sum/n (affected by outliers). Median = middle value (resistant). Mode = most frequent. Skew: mean > median → right skew.
IQR = Q3 − Q1. Outlier if outside Q1 − 1.5×IQR or Q3 + 1.5×IQR — quote the fence value in exams.

cards.front: Box plot — how to read the skew
cards.back: Median closer to the top of the box + long lower whisker → left/negative skew. Tail side = skew side.
Error = |measured − true|/true × 100. Change = (new − old)/old × 100. Different questions, don't mix.
−1 ≤ r ≤ 1: strength AND direction of LINEAR correlation. |r| > 0.8 strong. Correlation ≠ causation — always note it.

cards.front: Regression line — what is it for?
cards.back: Best-fit line for prediction. Interpolation (inside the data) is reliable; extrapolation (outside) is risky. Passes through (μx, μy).
Average spread about the mean. Larger SD = more variation. Additive to nothing — don't add SDs of two datasets directly.
0 ≤ P ≤ 1. P(not A) = 1 − P(A). Mutually exclusive: P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B).
P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A∩B) — subtract the overlap so it isn't counted twice.
P(A∩B) = P(A) × P(B) — and P(A|B) = P(A). Independence = no information shared.
P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B) — restrict the sample space to B first, then find A within it.
Multiply along branches (AND); add between complete paths (OR). Mark conditional branches after the first split.
Start from the INTERSECTION (both = 12) and work outwards — never fill the overlap first with one set's total.
Fixed n trials, two outcomes, constant p, independent trials. X ~ B(n, p).
E(X) = np — e.g. 50 flips of a fair coin → 25 heads expected.

cards.front: Binomial — P(X = r) and P(X ≥ r)
cards.back: P(X = r) = nCr·pʳ(1−p)^(n−r). 'At least r' = 1 − P(X ≤ r−1) — use the complement on the GDC.
Symmetric about the mean (mean = median = mode), bell-shaped, asymptotic tails, defined by μ and σ.
±1σ → 68% · ±2σ → 95% · ±3σ → 99.7%. Quote these when the GDC isn't needed.
normalcdf(lower, upper, μ, σ) for probabilities; invNorm(area, μ, σ) for x-values given a probability. Sketch and shade first.
